Ricardo Breceda's sculpture of a monster in the Anza-Borrego Desert Photo by Jim DeLillo In the remote desert outside Borrego Springs, California, monsters roam beneath some of the darkest skies in North America. They aren’t living beasts, but towering iron sculptures created by Mexican artist Ricardo Breceda. By day they loom like relics from another world. By night—under a band of stars—they transform into something surreal, almost alive.
The Artist and His Monsters Breceda began crafting his metal creatures after a construction accident left him seeking a new purpose. Encouraged by his daughter, he built his first dinosaur. Today, more than 130 sculptures dot the Anza-Borrego Desert, ranging from prehistoric mastodons to giant serpents and scorpions.
Iron Scorpion and Locust fight it out beneath the star,s Borrego Springs Photo by Jim DeLillo The collection sprawls across Galleta Meadows, private land where visitors are free to wander among the rust-colored giants. Unlike museum art, you can touch, climb near, and even picnic under them.
Nightfall in One of the Darkest Skies Borrego Springs is an International Dark Sky Community , making it a magnet for astrophotographers. As city lights fade, the Milky Way streaks across the heavens in vivid color. For photographers, the sculptures provide perfect foregrounds for night-sky compositions.
Even without a camera, the experience is unforgettable. Shadows stretch across the sand, coyotes howl in the distance, and the iron creatures take on eerie life.
Planning Your Visit A high-centered Jeep depicted in iron. Photo by Jim DeLillo Getting There: Borrego Springs is about two hours from San Diego or three hours from Los Angeles. When to Go: Spring offers wildflowers; summer nights are hot but bring the clearest skies. What to See: Don’t miss “The Serpent,” a 350-foot-long dragon that crosses the road, or the massive scorpion locked in combat with a grasshopper. Tips for Stargazing: Bring a flashlight, extra water, and a map—cell service is unreliable. Why It Matters In a world of curated Instagram spots, Borrego Springs feels raw and untamed. Standing alone in the dark desert, surrounded by monsters under the stars, is both humbling and exhilarating.
Whether you go for the art, the sky, or the sheer strangeness, Borrego Springs offers an unforgettable collision of imagination and wilderness.
